Cc: Andrew Li <andrew.li@bluenova.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — IP indemnity language concern

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we start contracting, our legal team flagged a concern in the proposed Order Form / MSA around third-party IP claims tied to AI-generated outputs. Two specific asks from BlueNova:

- Can you confirm whether the Customer indemnity is meant to cover claims arising from outputs produced by Redwood models (e.g., model hallucination that reproduces a third-party work)?
- If so, we need clearer notice/evidence obligations and a practical path for remediation — e.g., requested routing for evidence and a point of contact.

Our initial position is that BlueNova should not be on the hook for third-party claims when the output originates from Redwood model behavior independent of customer prompts or materials. We are open to a narrow carve-in for Customer Content we supply, but we need the wording to reflect that and to spell out the notice window and who receives evidence.

I've attached a short evidence checklist we use internally — we can fill it out once we have the redline.

Best,
Samantha Jones
Sr. Legal Ops 
BlueNova Therapeutics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — IP indemnity language concern

Samantha — thanks for the clear note and the checklist. Looping in Kim (legal) and Karthik (legal ops) to align on proposed language.

High level proposal from our side (so teams have a starting point):

- Narrow customer indemnity to Claims arising from Customer Materials or Customer-Provided Data (i.e., materials you upload/provide).
- Redwood will indemnify for direct third-party IP infringement caused by our delivery of a Model Output only where (i) the infringement is traceable to a specific identifiable output produced by the model and (ii) Redwood had notice and sole control of the defense (we can discuss defense allocation).
- Notice and evidence: 30 days to provide notice; customer to send initial claim and evidence to legal-evidence@bluenova.com and copy Redwood counsel; Redwood will provide a claim-response contact and an operations liaison for evidence ingestion.
- Remedies: we can discuss remediation scope; we propose limiting remediation to replacement, removal, or reasonable indemnity subject to the Order Form cap and exclusions (e.g., outputs that simply reproduce customer-provided licensed content).

I'll attach an initial order-form redline to make this concrete. Kim — could you take a pass on tightened redline alternatives (willful/negligent carve, training-data carveouts, and sample notice language)?

Next steps: Kim and Karthik to circulate redline by EOD; Ben will follow up with a proposed routing/contact for evidence ingest.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context — Ben and Samantha. I reviewed the draft redline and created a short memo with two alternative tracks for negotiation (attached):

Track A — Provider-limited carveout (more favorable to Redwood):
- Provider indemnifies only for direct third-party claims where the accused product is a literal copy from Redwood-controlled training data or where Redwood has willful infringement (very narrow).
- Customer indemnity remains limited to Customer Materials/Customer Data; Customer retains responsibility for prompts, prompts that include third-party content, and any sublicensing matters.

Track B — Mutual middle ground (recommended for most enterprise customers):
- Provider accepts indemnity for third-party claims arising from model outputs but only where Customer provides notice within 30 days and furnishes the evidence checklist. Redwood receives sole defense/control subject to cooperation obligations.
- Exclusions: outputs that reproduce licensed/attributed Customer Content; outputs produced after Customer used a custom prompt that included third-party materials; damages subject to the Order Form liability cap.

Key operational items to add to the Order Form: evidence routing instructions (single mailbox + S3 staging bucket for large media), a 30-day notice timeline for initial claim, and a defined liaison for triage. Those items reduce operational risk and are typical asks for customers in regulated verticals.

I've attached the redline notes with inline language and a short suggested clause for evidence routing (we propose: "Customer will submit claim notices and supporting materials to legal-evidence@bluenova.com; Redwood will provide a dedicated intake address for the claim-specific S3 staging path").

If BlueNova is open to Track B, I think we can agree quickly with a short Order Form addendum and playbook for evidence. If not, we'll iterate on A.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
